If it’s positive, you get two real solutions; if zero, one solution; if negative, complex solutions. Practice with simple examples to build confidence.

To find stationary points, take the derivative f’(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. Then plug those x-values back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates.
